reviews.text: Solid atmosphere piece but not really my thing. The writing is clean and Linnea is a well-drawn character, but nothing actually happens for most of the story. She measures silence, an inspector comes, she finds some old notebooks, she doesn't show him the secret room. The ending is her standing at a window watching a pigeon. I get that the point is the cost of obsession and all that, but I kept waiting for stakes to arrive and they never really did. The lost-time section was genuinely creepy though, and the detail about the notebook entries being better than hers was a sharp little knife. Just wish the story had more forward momentum.
